pr_title: network: do not always bump MTU with additional 4bytes
pr_comments: This makes more sense now. LGTM. Thanks.

issue_context.title: networkd: wrongly automatically increases MTU for a 4 bytes
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
> systemd 242 (242.29-1-arch)
+PAM +AUDIT -SELINUX -IMA -APPARMOR +SMACK -SYSVINIT +UTMP +LIBCRYPTSETUP +GCRYPT +GNUTLS +ACL +XZ +LZ4 +SECCOMP +BLKID +ELFUTILS +KMOD +IDN2 -IDN +PCRE2 default-hierarchy=hybrid

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released systemd versions upstream! -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Linux r1.opentech.local 5.0.13-arch1-1-ARCH #1 SMP PREEMPT Sun May 5 18:05:41 UTC 2019 x86_64 GNU/Linux

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > systemd-networkd is set user-defined MTU values.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > systemd-networkd is set MTU +4 bytes for underlayer interfaces.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

po1.netdev:
```
[NetDev]
Name=po1
Kind=bond
MTUBytes=1500

[Bond]
Mode=802.3ad
TransmitHashPolicy=layer2+3
LACPTransmitRate=fast
MIIMonitorSec=0.1
```

po1.network:
```
[Match]
Name=po1

[Network]
VLAN=vlan6
```

ten0.link:
```
[Match]
MACAddress=3c:fd:fe:aa:5e:f8

[Link]
Name=ten0
```

ten0.network:
```
[Match]
MACAddress=3c:fd:fe:aa:5e:f8

[Network]
Bond=po1
```

ten1.link:
```
[Match]
MACAddress=3c:fd:fe:aa:5e:f9

[Link]
Name=ten1
```

ten1.network:
```
[Match]
MACAddress=3c:fd:fe:aa:5e:f9

[Network]
Bond=po1
```

vlan6.netdev:
```
[NetDev]
Name=vlan6
Kind=vlan
MTUBytes=1500

[VLAN]
Id=6
```

vlan6.network:
```
[Match]
Name=vlan6

[Address]
Address=100.100.100.2/24
```
comments:
This is result:

![2019-05-13_16-03](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7759548/57609281-bf82a600-7598-11e9-8ccc-7f6fa29bc0ac.png)

But if MTUBytes is not declared, interfaces gets default MTU 1500byte's (as expected).
Seems this caused by #11807.

I'm not against this, but this may (and do!) break some systems on upgrade:
![2019-05-13_16-10](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7759548/57610164-77648300-759a-11e9-9982-738780c0b811.png)

On our luck this router (40km from city) have second NIC on LACP with another chip with support MTU more than 1500.
I think this "+4 byte for vlan automatically" may be switched off by some parameter and enabled by default. @yuwata?
@k0ste Thank you for the report. I hope #12574 fixes the issue.

review_comments: Why we are bumping up the MTU. Should not the user responsible for this ? I think this kind of conf should be handled by the user and let kernel deicides.
Otherwise, vlan devices may not work... Of course, just warning about that may be ok. But, when we know what is a minimal requirement, then I think it may be helpful to bump MTU.
And if we do not bump MTU, then user may not find why vlan does not work. See #5972.
For that we just need to log it and should not increase.
